title: Error Practice
goal: This lesson covers how to spot, catch, and fix errors in short programs, and how to choose between fixing and catching.
learn: Use try and except with friendly messages
Fix the root cause when you can
idea: Practice time. Sometimes you fix the bug, which is the best option. Other times you catch a risk you cannot avoid, like bad text turning into a number. Read the message, choose between fixing and catching, and keep the program kind to the next person who runs it.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the first value from "10" to "5" and press Run. The first result should be 20.0.

practice.text: Loop ['3','0','x']. For each, try 9/int(item). Catch ValueError and ZeroDivisionError with different messages.
practice.hint: Inside try:, print(9 / int(item)). "3" works, "0" hits ZeroDivisionError, and "x" hits ValueError. Give each except its own message.
practice.starterTip: In try: add print(9 / int(item)). In except blocks try print("Not a number!") and print("Cannot divide by zero!").
practice.gradingNote: Pass if 3.0 prints, zero-divide is caught, and x triggers ValueError message.

practice.text: Fix the NameError (do not use try). Print the sum of a and b.
practice.hint: There is no variable c, only a and b. The sum of 4 and 6 should be 10.
practice.starterTip: Change print(a + c) to print(a + b). No try/except needed, just fix the typo.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if print uses a + b and shows 10 with no error.

quiz.question: When should you fix instead of catch?

options.text: When the bug is a simple mistake you control

quiz.correct: Right, typos should be fixed and risky input can be caught.
quiz.wrong: Choose the right tool for the job.

quiz.question: Can one try have more than one except?
quiz.correct: Yes, you can stack specific except blocks for different error types.
quiz.wrong: ValueError and ZeroDivisionError can both appear.

quiz.question: What is the goal of error practice?

options.text: Programs that fail softly and stay clear

quiz.correct: Right, clear handling builds your confidence.

project.title: Error Detective
project.desc: Build a tiny tool that tries to convert each of '8', '0', and 'hi' and prints 16 / n. Use specific excepts and end with All checked.
